key_insight: Stitching artifacts from patch-based generation can quietly degrade downstream segmentation, and artifact-free 3D stitching only modestly improves results over 2D despite higher cost.
clinical_relevance: For biomedical imaging pipelines, the main takeaway is that image quality metrics alone may miss errors that affect automated analysis, so downstream task performance should be checked.
method: Compared 3 stitching approaches for patch assembly
Benchmarked 2D vs 3D cycleGANs on cryo-EM data
Evaluated both perceptual quality and mitochondria segmentation performance
evidence_signal: FID did not reliably detect subtle stitching artifacts, but those artifacts significantly changed downstream segmentation performance.
watch_item: The reported 3D gains were small relative to added compute, so implementation choices should balance artifact control against hardware and training cost.
paper_title: Stitching and dimensionality effects on large artificially generated volume datasets
